data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic elements 'adal' meaning 'noble' and 'heid' meaning 'head' or 'kind, type'. This name was popular among the Germanic peoples and was borne by several early Christian saints. The name Adalheid represents the nobility of character and the strength and courage of the soul. The name Adalheid carries the meaning “Noble, Nobility” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Adalheid usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, nobility and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: אדלהיד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אדלהיד הוא מילה גרמנית עתיקה שמורכבת משתי מילים: 'אדאל' שפירושו אציל, ו'הייד' שפירושו יופי או צורה. הוא מתאר את היופי והאצילות של אלוהים, ומשמש כזכר לאיכות האלוהית והשמימית.

in_greek.name: Αδαλχέιδ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αδαλχέιδ προέρχεται από την αρχαία γερμανική γλώσσα και αποτελείται από δύο λέξεις: 'αδάλ' που σημαίνει ευγενής, και 'χέιδ' που σημαίνει ομορφιά ή μορφή. Εκφράζει την ευγενεία και την ομορφιά του Θεού, και χρησιμεύει ως υπενθύμιση της θεϊκής και ουράνιας ποιότητας.

in_latin.name: Adalheid
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Adalheid ex lingua germanica antiqua derivatur, compositum ex duobus vocabulis: 'adal' quod significat nobilitas, et 'heid' quod significat pulchritudo seu forma. Designat nobilitatem et pulchritudinem Dei, ac servit ad recordationem qualitatis divinae et caelestis.

in_english.name: Adalheid
in_english.meaning: Nobility and beauty of God, divine beauty and nobility
in_english.long_meaning: The name Adalheid originates from Old High German, composed of 'adal' meaning noble and 'heid' meaning beauty or form. It signifies the nobility and beauty of God, reflecting divine qualities. Historically used in Christian tradition, it symbolizes spiritual nobility and elegance. The name conveys a sense of sacred beauty and aristocratic virtues, cherished in Christian cultures.
